Pipeline stage: assemble fixed test forms

Source: R/pipeline-forms.R
assemble_forms.Rd

Builds one or more fixed test forms from the calibrated items with automated test assembly (mixed-integer programming through the eatATA package). The items come from the pipeline's item bank (bank_items()) if it has one, otherwise from the calibrated model. Each form has length items, meets the content blueprint, keeps enemy items apart, and the forms are made as informative as possible at the theta points: with one form the information summed over theta is maximized, with several forms the smallest of the forms' sums is maximized, which keeps them parallel.

Usage

assemble_forms(
  p,
  length,
  n_forms = 1,
  theta = c(-1, 0, 1),
  content = NULL,
  blueprint = NULL,
  enemies = NULL,
  max_use = 1,
  solver = c("GLPK", "lpSolve"),
  time_limit = 20
)

Arguments

p

a calibrated pipeline from calibrate().

length

number of items per form.

n_forms

number of forms.

theta

ability points (on the bank scale) where the forms should be most informative, such as a cut score.

content

optional content category of each item: a named vector (names are item names).

blueprint

the number of items per content category on each form: a named vector of exact counts, or a data frame with columns category, min and max. Needs content.

enemies

optional pairs of items that must not appear on the same form: a list of character vectors of length two, or a two-column matrix.

max_use

the number of forms an item may appear on (1 means no overlap between forms).

solver

solver used by eatATA: "GLPK" (default) or "lpSolve".

time_limit

time limit for the solver, in seconds.

Value

The pipeline with p$forms (a list with method = "ata", items, a tibble with one row per form and item, and info, a tibble of test information and SEM per form at each theta).

Details

The checks (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • no_solution (block): no set of forms meets every constraint; relax the blueprint, shorten the forms or allow items on more than one form (max_use).

  • blueprint (block): a form's content counts fall outside the blueprint.

  • enemy_items (block): two enemy items on one form.

  • parallel_forms (review): the forms' test information at a theta point differs by more than parallel_tol (relative to the largest).

  • form_precision (review): the standard error of measurement of a form at a theta point is above cat_sem.

  • not_optimal (info): the solver found forms that meet every constraint but ran out of time before proving they are the most informative ones; a longer time_limit may give slightly better forms.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("eatATA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  p <- add_responses(mv_pipeline(), certexam, items = 3:34, key = certexam_key)
  p <- calibrate(drop_items(p, "Q14"), model = "2PL")
  p <- assemble_forms(p, length = 12, n_forms = 2, theta = 0)
  p$forms$info
}
